research: [spread] Line movement: Chicago opened -1.5 and moved to -3 (Patriots +3 -118) even though the public splits were on New England (63% / 78% NE, WagerTalk/GoldSheet, Oct 20). That is a reverse move toward the favorite, which helps CHI on paper, but LESSONS says moves toward the favorite have gone 1-4.

[spread] Covers (Joe Osborne, updated Oct 22, 6:25 PM ET) listed Bears -3.5 on game day, and Covers' early leans (Oct 19) had -2.5. The market settled about -3 to -3.5, so the slate's -3 is only half a point better for the Bears side. That is under the 1+ point slate edge LESSONS asks for, so it is neutral.
[spread] New England is 5-0 ATS and 4-1 straight up in regular-season prime-time games under Mike Vrabel (Covers, Oct 22). Helps NE, but ATS records are priced and are a tiebreaker at most.
[spread] Sportsgambler (Oct 21-22): NE covered 8 of its last 10 and 9 of its last 10 on the road; Chicago covered 5 of its last 10 and 7 of 10 at home. Helps NE, but priced.
[spread] Efficiency: New England's season yards-per-play differential is positive and Chicago's is negative (Covers, Oct 22). Helps NE.

Chicago's pass defense ranks near the bottom in yards allowed per play and 31st in yards allowed per pass attempt. It has allowed a league-high eight pass plays of 40+ yards and plays man coverage at the second-highest rate (Covers, Oct 22). Helps NE against Maye's recent form.

Drake Maye has 10 TD passes and 1 INT over NE's three-game win streak, and NE averaged 33.3 points in it: 29-26 over Buffalo, 45-17 over Las Vegas, 26-19 over the Jets (Covers Oct 22; Sportsgambler). Covers' Jason Logan (Oct 19) notes those came against softer defenses. Helps NE, with a caveat.

[angle] New England's offensive line is battered: Will Campbell, Alijah Vera-Tucker, Ben Brown and Morgan Moses are all dealing with injuries, and both starting guards were reported out (WagerTalk Oct 20; Covers Oct 22). WR Romeo Doubs is on IR (shoulder) and A.J. Brown is back from an ankle injury. Helps CHI.

[angle] Chicago's pass rush: Kyler Gordon made his season debut at Atlanta with 3 sacks and 2 forced fumbles, the Bears had 5 sacks that game, and Covers' Logan calls the rush blitz-heavy. DE Montez Sweat is suspended for PEDs pending appeal (WagerTalk Oct 20). Mostly helps CHI, offset by losing Sweat.

Caleb Williams returned from a hamstring injury and went 30-of-36 for 305 yards in a 31-23 win at Atlanta. RB Kyle Monangai (toe) was hopeful to return after missing two games (WagerTalk Oct 20; Covers Oct 19). Helps CHI.
[angle] Short week: Thursday road trip for NE, and Logan (Covers, Oct 19) argues it hurts Maye behind a depleted line. NE also 'continues to struggle with fumbles' (WagerTalk). Helps CHI.

Form is volatile on both sides. Bears: lost 3-9 to Minnesota, beat Philadelphia 27-7, beat the Jets 23-12, lost 7-31 to Green Bay, won 31-23 at Atlanta. Patriots: beat Pittsburgh 20-3, lost 6-35 at Jacksonville, then won three straight (Sportsgambler). Neutral.
Weather: clear, about 60F, wind about 5 mph (Covers, Oct 22). Neutral. Total 50.5, moved up from a 48.5 open on public Over money (WagerTalk).
games.reasoning: Before the leak the evidence was close to balanced. The market moved from Chicago -1.5 to -3/-3.5 against public New England money, while NE's efficiency edge and Chicago's leaky pass defense pointed the other way. My projection sat at about the line (Bears by 3), with no 2+ point shaded edge, so this was a pass. The [angle] that stood out was NE's line injuries (both starting guards) against a Bears rush that just had 5 sacks. Contamination forces a pass per LESSONS in any case. Forced side is the underdog, New England: LESSONS on favorites, NFL road teams covering, and moves toward the favorite not holding.
games.contaminationNote: I fetched the Sportsgambler preview (dated Oct 21-22) for its pre-game content. Its standings table showed current records of Patriots 5-5 and Bears 8-2, against 4-2 for both teams before this game. That implies Chicago won this game, margin unknown. I saw it before writing any lean. I locked a pass as LESSONS requires. The forced side (NE) comes from the pre-leak reasoning (underdog, road team, the move toward the favorite) and runs against what the leak hints.
